## Task 1

#Environment setup and data combination

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

# Merge the 2 datasets

```{r}
d1=read.table("student-mat.csv",sep=";",header=TRUE)
d2=read.table("student-por.csv",sep=";",header=TRUE)

#Using the original code
j0=merge(d1,d2,by=c("school","sex","age","address","famsize","Pstatus","Medu","Fedu","Mjob","Fjob","reason","nursery","internet"))
print(nrow(d3)) # 382 students

#using inner join()
id_keys <- c(
  "school","sex","age","address","famsize","Pstatus",
  "Medu","Fedu","Mjob","Fjob","reason","nursery","internet"
)

j1 <- inner_join(
  d1, d2,
  by = id_keys,
  suffix = c(".math", ".por")
)

nrow(j1)     # should be 382 (same as your base::merge)
names(j1)    # you'll see G1.math, G1.por, etc.
```

# Inner-join on all shared columns except G1, G2, G3, paid, absences
```{r}
drop_cols <- c("G1","G2","G3","paid","absences")
by_excl5  <- setdiff(intersect(names(d1), names(d2)), drop_cols)

combined <- inner_join(d1, d2, by = by_excl5, suffix = c(".math", ".por"))

nrow(combined)   # check matches 
```

#Pick four categorical variables and convert them to factors in
- the math table (d1),
-the Portuguese table (d2), and
-the combined table you just created
```{r}
cat_vars <- c("school","sex","address","famsize")

to_factor <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(across(all_of(cat_vars), ~ factor(.x)))
}

d1_fac       <- to_factor(d1)        # math
d2_fac       <- to_factor(d2)        # Portuguese
combined_fac <- to_factor(combined)  # joined table to use in later tasks

# quick sanity check
sapply(d1_fac[cat_vars], is.factor)
sapply(d2_fac[cat_vars], is.factor)
sapply(combined_fac[cat_vars], is.factor)
```
